headline: GOLD SLIPS TO $4,307 AS FED HIKES 25 BPS — First Rate Increase Since 2023 Firms Dollar; Silver Falls 1.1% to $65.27
snippet: The Federal Reserve hiked its policy rate 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% in a unanimous vote — its first tightening since 2023 — while 16 of 18 officials signalled further increases may follow, driving the US Dollar Index above 100 to a one-year peak. Gold spot fell 0.81% to $4,307.63 and silver dropped 1.11% to $65.27, snapping silver's run to a weekly high from Tuesday; St. Louis Fed President Musalem said rates 'may need to go higher still' and Chicago's Goolsbee flagged persistent supply shocks as a reason for continued vigilance.

headline: TRUMP-XI SUMMIT OPENS TODAY — China's Nov. 10 Rare Earth Export Control Deadline Hangs Over White House Talks
snippet: Xi Jinping arrives at the White House on September 24 for his first visit since 2008, with China's suspension of sweeping rare earth export controls set to expire November 10 — a deadline analysts say has made Trump unusually restrained ahead of the meeting. China's rare earth exports to the US fell 20% in the months leading up to the summit, and Beijing has already added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export control entity list; critical minerals and AI safeguards are expected to dominate the agenda alongside tariff talks.

headline: RED LAKE BONANZA: 925.52 g/t AU OVER 1m IN INTACT PANEL — West Red Lake Madsen Mine Austin 904 Eyes 2027 Integration
source_name: GlobeNewswire / West Red Lake Gold Mines
snippet: West Red Lake Gold Mines (TSXV: WRLG) reported drill results from the Madsen Mine including a headline 176.04 g/t Au over 5.3 metres — with a 1-metre bonanza sub-interval at 925.52 g/t Au associated with visible gold and biotite alteration — and 128.32 g/t Au over 4.5 metres, from the Austin 955 and 904 Complexes at 600–700 metres depth in the Red Lake District. The Austin 904 is a 200 × 200 metre panel of intact, historically unmined gold mineralization; management confirmed these results build confidence in integrating both panels into the Madsen mine plan in 2027.

headline: NEXGOLD INTERSECTS 14.07 g/t AU OVER 7m AT GOLDLUND — Ontario Deposit Expanding in 35,000m Campaign
snippet: NexGold Mining Corp (TSXV: NEXG) reported results from 10 diamond drill holes at the Goldlund Deposit within its Goliath Gold Complex in Ontario, highlighted by 14.07 g/t Au over 7.0 metres, 9.76 g/t Au over 8.0 metres and 2.84 g/t Au over 13.0 metres — with 31,971 metres of its expanded 35,000-metre program now complete. Goldlund is one of three deposits within the Goliath Gold Complex and continues to add mineralized strike and depth ahead of a resource update.

headline: INVENTUS FINDS BULK-TONNAGE GOLD 2.7m FROM SURFACE — Pardo Phase 2 Done; 100 Holes In, Maiden Resource Q4 2026
snippet: Inventus Mining Corp (TSXV: IVS) released Phase 2 results from its Pardo 'River of Gold' Project, 65 km northeast of Sudbury, Ontario, reporting 100 drill holes including a high of 4.96 g/t Au over 2.09 metres beginning just 2.72 metres from surface (with a 30.04 g/t Au sub-interval over 0.33 m) across multiple stacked paleoplacer gold-bearing layers. Phase 3 drilling begins mid-October; a maiden mineral resource estimate is targeted for Q4 2026 — the next major de-risking step for a self-funded Ontario junior operating its own 100-tpd bulk sampling plant.

headline: MIDLAND/SOQUEM FIND 26.8% COPPER IN BOULDER — New Showings Open 4km Cu-Au-Ag Corridor in Quebec's Labrador Trough
snippet: Midland Exploration Inc. (TSXV: MD) and SOQUEM Inc. announced the discovery of new copper-gold-silver boulders returning up to 26.8% Cu, 0.87 g/t Au and 238 g/t Ag from veins hosted in monzonite dykes at the Nachicapau project in Nunavik, Quebec, plus two new outcrop showings assaying up to 3.03% Cu, 0.77 g/t Au and 20 g/t Ag. Results extend the footprint of a 4-km-long by 1.5-km-wide copper-gold-silver corridor defined between 2022 and 2025 under the Midland-SOQUEM Strategic Alliance in the Labrador Trough — a geologically underexplored corridor with no resource-stage projects yet.

headline: ANGLOGOLD STAKES $100M EARN-IN AS KINCORA HITS 4 NEW PORPHYRY COMPLEXES — 40km NSW Strike Confirms Province Scale
snippet: Kincora Copper (TSXV/ASX: KCC) reported that four scout holes at its Nevertire South licence in NSW uncovered four potential new porphyry copper-gold complexes — grades anomalous for proximity to a porphyry system centre — across a prospective strike now exceeding 40 kilometres in the covered Northern Junee-Narromine Belt. AngloGold Ashanti Australia has the right to invest up to A$100 million across five adjacent Kincora licences spanning over 100 km, with Kincora managing all programs for a 10% fee; assay results from the Condobolin licence are pending as the next near-term catalyst.

headline: DRILL RESULTS JAMMED IN 75-DAY LAB QUEUES — Capital Deployed Q2-Q3 Points to Concentrated Q4 Reporting Burst
snippet: Assay turnaround times for junior mining companies have degraded to as long as 75 days from a pre-pandemic baseline of roughly 20 days, with capital deployed into drilling through Q2 and Q3 2026 now sitting in lab queues across the sector. The bottleneck points to a concentrated reporting burst expected through Q4 2026 and into January 2027 — creating an unusually compressed catalyst window for retail investors who began accumulating positions on exploration plays earlier this year.

headline: RECORD AUSSIE DRILLING MASKS SHRINKING DISCOVERY PIPELINE — More Metres, Fewer Deposits Since 2018
snippet: Australia set a record for mineral exploration drilling expenditure in the first half of 2026, yet the number of new significant discoveries per dollar deployed has fallen sharply since the 2018 cycle peak — a divergence that analysts attribute to rising costs, shallower remaining near-surface targets, and a shift toward infill rather than greenfields programs. For investors screening exploration juniors, the data argues strongly for prioritising companies with genuine greenfields exposure in underexplored terrains over those simply expanding known deposits.

headline: CAMECO FLOODS + KAZATOMPROM CUTS COMPOUND URANIUM DEFICIT — Saskatchewan Disruption Widens Supply Squeeze at $96.50 Term Price
snippet: Cameco halted its Key Lake mill and reduced McArthur River output after flooding disrupted supply routes in northern Saskatchewan, adding a near-term supply shock on top of Kazatomprom's 8-million-pound guidance cut — together removing a combined estimated 12+ million pounds from 2026 global supply into a market where the long-term uranium contract price already touched a nominal all-time record of US$96.50/lb in September. Spot uranium at $89.70/lb remains well below the term price, signalling that utilities are locking in supply at elevated term prices while spot remains constrained by lack of discretionary pounds.
